Name: Regeneron ISEF
Description: The Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair (ISEF) is the world’s largest international pre-college science competition. Each year, more than 1,600 high-school students from nearly every state in the U.S. and more than 60 countries, regions, and territories compete at Society-affiliated fairs to win the opportunity to attend ISEF. These top young scientific minds come together to showcase their talent on an international stage, be judged by doctoral-level scientists, and compete for more than $9 million in awards during ISEF.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific rigor, hypothesis novelty, data integrity, oral defense, Student with university-lab grade original research and experimental mastery, ,

Name: Research Science Institute (RSI) MIT
Description:
RSI is arguably the world's most competitive research summer programme for high schoolers, with an acceptance rate well below 1%. Each summer, 100 of the world's most accomplished high school students gather at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) for the Research Science Institute (RSI). In 2027, CEE is expanding the RSI to Stanford for 50 young scholars. RSI is the first cost-free to students, summer science & engineering program to combine on-campus course work in scientific theory with off-campus work in science and technology research.
Participants experience the entire research cycle from start to finish. They read the most current literature in their field, execute a detailed research plan, and deliver conference-style oral and written reports on their findings. RSI scholars first participate in a week of intensive STEM classes with accomplished professors. The heart of RSI is the five week research internship where students conduct individual projects under the tutelage of mentors who are experienced scientists and researchers. During the final week of RSI, students prepare written and oral presentations on their research projects.
Evaluation_Criteria: Academic excellence, Olympiad track record, STEM agency, original inquiry, Top 1% STEM profile with Olympiad scores (USAMO/USACO) and established research trajectory, ,

Name: Research Science Institute (RSI) IISc
Description: RSI-India is a six-week intensive summer STEM research and enrichment program that is cost-free for Indian secondary school students of exceptionally strong academic ability and potential. It is an extension of the RSI programme hosted annually at MIT & Stanford. Thirty-two students will be selected based on their completed applications containing written personal statements, achievements in STEM fields, exam scores, letters of recommendation, and school transcripts. Selected students will be matched with a research mentor at the IISc, where they will attend courses for the first week, complete individual hands-on research projects with their IISc mentors, and then present a paper and a talk on their research at the RSI-India Student Symposium during the final week. In addition to the academic aspect of RSI-India, students will hear distinguished invited speakers at the Palsamudram Lecture Series, named in honor of Mr. Sanjay Palsamudram, founder of the Palsamudram Trust, a technology investor and mentor from Bengaluru. Students will meet and connect with other talented students from across the nation, fostering friendships and collaborations that will last for decades. Social activities round out the program.
Evaluation_Criteria: Academic merit, conceptual grasp in basic sciences, research curiosity, Top Indian science students preparing for national research careers, ,

Name: Regeneron Science Talent Search (STS)
Description: Regeneron STS is the nation’s oldest and most prestigious science research competition for high school students. Started in 1942 as the Westinghouse Science Talent Search, Regeneron STS recognizes and empowers our nation’s most promising young scientists who are developing ideas that could solve society’s most urgent challenges.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific depth, individual agency, societal significance, leadership record, High school senior with exceptional independent research paper and extracurricular profile, ,

Name: USA Computing Olympiad (USACO)
Description:
The USACO supports computing education in the USA and worldwide by identifying, motivating, and training high-school computing students at all levels. We provide hundreds of hours of free on-line training resources and historical contest problems (complete with solutions) that students can use to improve their programming and computational problem-solving skills, on-line programming contests (four per year) for students at all levels, an intensive summer training camp, to which the top students in the USA are invited to further improve their skills and learn advanced material.
The opportunity for the top four students in the USA to represent their country at the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI), the most prestigious international algorithmic programming competition at the high-school level. We also select a team of the top four female high-school students in the USA to compete at the European Girls' Olympiad in Informatics (EGOI), a competition of similar prestige modeled after the European Girls' Mathematical Olympiad.
Evaluation_Criteria: Algorithmic efficiency, computational speed, time/space complexity optimization, Elite algorithmic problem solver fluent in advanced graph theory dynamic programming and C++, ,

Name: Thiel Fellowship
Description: Founded by technology entrepreneur and investor Peter Thiel in 2011, the Thiel Fellowship is a two-year program for young people who want to build new things. Thiel Fellows skip or stop out of college to receive a $250,000 grant and support from the Thiel Foundation’s network of founders, investors, and scientists.
Evaluation_Criteria: Founder conviction, technical velocity, defensible IP, commercial traction, Visionary with extreme agency who has shipped an early prototype or revenue-generating company, ,

Name: John Locke Essay Competition
Description:
The John Locke Institute encourages young people to cultivate the characteristics that turn good students into great writers: independent thought, depth of knowledge, clear reasoning, critical analysis and persuasive style. The Essay Competition invites students to explore a wide range of challenging and interesting questions beyond the confines of the school curriculum.
Entering an essay in the competition will build knowledge, and refine skills of argumentation. It also gives students the chance to have their work assessed by experts. All of the essay prizes are judged by a panel of senior academics drawn from leading universities including Oxford, Cambridge, Harvard, Princeton, and Stanford, under the leadership of the Chairman of Examiners, Prof. Terence Kealey.
The judges will select the 1st, 2nd, and 3rd prizewinners from each of the ten subject categories - Economics, History, International Relations, Law, Philosophy, Politics, Psychology, Public Policy, Science & Technology, and Theology - and then select the winner of the Grand Prize for the best entry in any subject.
Evaluation_Criteria: Intellectual rigor, clarity of argumentation, original counter-examples, prose style, Philosophically mature writer capable of rigorous dialectic analysis beyond high school syllabi, ,

Name: The Concord Review
Description: The Concord Review, Inc., was founded in March 1987 to recognize and to publish exemplary history essays by high school students in the English-speaking world. With the Fall Issue (#137), more than 1,500 research papers (average 8,500 words, with endnotes and bibliography) have been published from authors in 46 states and 46 other countries. The Concord Review remains the only quarterly journal in the world to publish the academic history papers of secondary students.
Evaluation_Criteria: Archival research depth, Chicago-style citation rigor, narrative nuance, Meticulous student historian willing to draft an exhaustive 4000-8000 word footnoted monograph, ,

Name: Scholastic Art & Writing Awards
Description:
The Alliance for Young Artists & Writers identifies and supports the next generation of creative voices. Founded to preserve the legacy and shepherd the future of the Scholastic Art & Writing Awards, the Alliance activates a vibrant network of teen artists and writers, alumni, and educational partners across the United States and Canada; creates opportunities for recognition, exhibition, publication, scholarships, and community-building; and celebrates the transformative power of creative expression. 
In 2026, more than 110,000 teens across the United States and Canada entered nearly 335,000 original works in 29 different categories of art and writing.
Evaluation_Criteria: Originality, authentic voice, mastery of craft, creative risk-taking, Evocative creative writer with distinct personal voice and polished literary execution, ,

Name: Wharton Global Youth Investment Challenge
Description: The Wharton Global High School Investment Competition is a free, experiential investment challenge for high school students (9th to 12th grade) and teachers. Students work in teams of four to six, guided by a teacher from their school as their advisor, and have access to an online stock market simulator. Together, they learn about strategy-building, teamwork, communication, risk, diversification, company and industry analysis, and many other aspects of investing.
Evaluation_Criteria: Portfolio strategy rationale, adherence to client goals, financial analysis depth, Analytical team skilled in equity research, financial modeling, and investment thesis generation, ,

Name: Ready Trader Go (Optiver)
Description:
Optiver Ready Trader Go is a premier global algorithmic student trading competition hosted by the proprietary trading firm Optiver. Participants build a quantitative trading algorithm to market-make and execute trades in a simulated exchange environment, competing for substantial cash prizes.
The challenge typically requires teams to trade a highly correlated liquid Future contract against an illiquid ETF. Competitors must manage inventory, respond to shifting market volatility, and optimize the bid-ask spread to maximize profit while minimizing risk exposure.
Evaluation_Criteria: Profitability, latency optimization, risk management, market shock resilience, Mathematically sharp programmer fluent in probability simulation structures and quantitative logic, ,

Name: Conrad Challenge
Description:
The Conrad Challenge invites high school students ages 13-18 to present their STEM inventions to a panel of expert judges, after months of rigorous planning and strategizing their innovation and business model. 
Since its inception, the Conrad Challenge has engaged over 1,000 schools from all 50 U.S. states and 72 countries, reinforcing the commitment to diversity and global representation. The 2024-2025 competition saw record-breaking participation with over 4,400 students involved.
Evaluation_Criteria: Market viability, prototype functional maturity, IP defensibility, pitch delivery, Cross-disciplinary team combining technical engineering with sound business fundamentals, ,

Name: Diamond Challenge
Description: The Diamond Challenge is a global entrepreneurship competition for high school students (ages 14–18), created and hosted annually by Horn Entrepreneurship at the University of Delaware. It empowers teens to identify pressing real-world problems, build original business or social venture concepts, and compete for over $100,000 in cash and awards.
Evaluation_Criteria: Customer discovery validation, feasibility, unit economics, scalable systemic impact, Resourceful student entrepreneur who has validated ideas with real target customer interviews, ,

Name: Technovation Girls
Description: Technovation Girls is a free technology-based program for girls ages 10 - 18. Working in teams (of 1 to 5), girls find a problem in their community and build a mobile app to help solve it. Along the way, they develop their collaboration, problem-solving, and leadership skills. Technovation Girls will take 30+ hours to complete (we recommend allocated about 12 weeks to finish) and is completely free.
Evaluation_Criteria: Mobile app architecture, community problem-solution fit, business plan coherence, All-female student team eager to learn coding while directly addressing local community pain points, ,

Name: MIT THINK Scholars Program
Description: The MIT THINK Scholars Program is a national science, research, and innovation competition for high school students in the United States, organized and judged by undergraduates at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Instead of requiring a completed research project, THINK evaluates early-stage, well-researched written proposals for original STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Math) projects.
Evaluation_Criteria: Novelty, feasibility, resource planning, realistic execution within semester scope, Ambitious student with a well-scoped engineering/science proposal lacking institutional lab access, ,

Name: Apple Swift Student Challenge
Description: The Apple Swift Student Challenge is an annual global coding competition that empowers student developers to showcase their technical skills, innovation, and creativity. Participants are tasked with creating an interactive app playground using Apple's Swift programming language, designed to solve a problem or share a meaningful story.
Evaluation_Criteria: UI/UX design, originality, Swift architecture, accessibility integration, Individual developer with a creative app idea displaying empathy, accessibility, and Swift fluency, ,

Name: Congressional App Challenge
Description: Every year we challenge students in our districts to create and submit their original apps for a chance to win the Congressional App Challenge (CAC). Each challenge is district-specific. As U.S. Representatives we publicly recognize our winning teams and each winning app may be put on display in the U.S. Capitol Building for one year. Additional prizes may be available. The Congressional Internet Caucus initiates the annual CAC. We have appointed the non-profit Internet Education Foundation to provide the CAC with supplemental staffing and support.
Evaluation_Criteria: Civic applicability, code functionality, user accessibility, explanatory video clarity, Self-taught hacker addressing community issues via web mobile or desktop software applications, ,

Name: PennApps
Description: Since 2009, PennApps has brought students from across the country to Penn for a weekend of building, learning, and launching ideas. For our twenty-seventh mission, we’re touching down in the desert, so grab your crew and join the expedition.
Evaluation_Criteria: Technical complexity, design completeness, novelty, live demo presentation, Rapid product prototyper comfortable shipping full-stack apps or AI workflows in 36 hours, ,

Name: FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC)
Description: Starting with a Kit of Parts, teams of high school students design, program, and build industrial-sized robots to play an action-packed game, released in January. They compete on a themed field as part of a three-team alliance in the spirit of Coopertition®. In 360-degree learning guided by adult mentors, each FIRST® Robotics Competition team also creates a team identity, raises funds to meet its goals, and advances appreciation for STEM in its community.
Evaluation_Criteria: Mechanical design, electrical reliability, autonomous pathing, alliance strategy, Hands-on builder skilled in CAD machining, Java/C++ robot control, or alliance scouting, ,

Name: Queen's Commonwealth Essay Competition
Description: The Queen's Commonwealth Writing Competition (formerly the Queen's Commonwealth Essay Competition) is the world's oldest international writing contest for schools, run by the Royal Commonwealth Society since 1883.
Evaluation_Criteria: Literary style, originality, alignment with commonwealth theme, emotional cadence, Articulate Commonwealth student writer capable of reframing global themes into vivid prose, ,

Name: Foyle Young Poets Award
Description: The Foyle Young Poets of the Year Award is the world’s leading international poetry competition for young writers aged 11 to 17, run annually by The Poetry Society and supported by the Foyle Foundation. The top 15 winners receive a week-long residential writing course with the Arvon Foundation, publication in an anthology, and mentoring/internship opportunities. All 100 winners receive a year’s youth membership to The Poetry Society and book collections.
Evaluation_Criteria: Fresh imagery, emotional authenticity, meter/free-verse discipline, distinct voice, Young poet with an original evocative voice unencumbered by formulaic academic constraints, ,

Name: Harvard International Economics Essay Contest (HIEEC)
Description: HIEEC invites high-school students worldwide to take a position on a current economic question and defend it in a focused essay, giving them an opportunity to showcase their analytical writing skills and understanding of economic concepts. This is our largest program, drawing hundreds of essays from dozens of countries each year.
Evaluation_Criteria: Economic intuition, real-world data integration, empirical citation quality, logic, Aspiring economist who can translate micro/macro frameworks into compelling policy critique, ,

Name: Smart India Hackathon (SIH)
Description:
Smart India Hackathon (SIH) is a premier nationwide initiative designed to engage students in solving some of the most pressing challenges faced in everyday life. Launched to foster a culture of innovation and practical problem-solving, SIH provides a dynamic platform for students to develop and showcase their creative solutions to real-world problems. By encouraging participants to think critically and innovatively, the hackathon aims to bridge the gap between academic knowledge and practical application.
Since its inception, SIH has garnered significant success in promoting out-of-the-box thinking among young minds, particularly engineering students from across India. Each edition has built on the previous one, refining its approach and expanding its impact. The hackathon not only offers students an opportunity to showcase their skills but also encourages collaboration with industry experts, government agencies, and other stakeholders.
Evaluation_Criteria: System architecture, real-world viability, cost efficiency, public policy fit, Indian tech student adept at building rapid functional prototypes solving public governance issues, ,

Name: Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Bal Puraskar
Description: India's highest civilian honor for children displaying extraordinary talent and societal impact.
Evaluation_Criteria: National-level extraordinary achievement, documented third-party proof, resilience, Prodigious Indian youth who has made monumental contributions in innovation, bravery, or arts, ,

Name: The Diana Award
Description: The Diana Award is an international award that honours young people who work to improve the lives of others. Named after Diana, Princess of Wales, the Diana Award was established in 1999 by a board chaired by Gordon Brown.
Evaluation_Criteria: Vision, social impact, youth leadership journey, sustained service resilience, Dedicated grassroots changemaker who has led an impactful humanitarian campaign for 12+ months, ,

Name: Emergent Ventures Grant (Mercatus Center)
Description: Emergent Ventures is a low-overhead fellowship and grant program administered by Mercatus Center Faculty Director Tyler Cowen, supporting thinkers and doers worldwide who pursue highly scalable, “zero to one” ideas to meaningfully improve society., bold research, and agency.
Evaluation_Criteria: Agency, originality, scalability of idea, execution speed, high-upside potential, Hyper-driven self-directed learner pursuing unconventional breakthroughs without waiting for credentials

Name: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow
Description: The Samsung Solve for Tomorrow competition asks students to consider how science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) can be used to create change in their communities. With the help of their teachers, students compete to win up to $50,000 in prizes for their school, plus the opportunity to work with Samsung employees to develop their innovations. Solve for Tomorrow is now powered by MIT Solve. Click below to learn more about eligibility and how to get started.
Evaluation_Criteria: Community impact, STEM application feasibility, engaging stakeholder storytelling, Civic-minded STEM team capable of engaging local leaders to build real-world implementations, ,

Name: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow India
Description: The Samsung Solve for Tomorrow competition asks students to consider how science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) can be used to create change in their communities. The SST India contest offers generous incubation grants and IIT Delhi mentoring.
Evaluation_Criteria: Social impact, technological viability, environmental/societal scalability, Indian engineering/high school innovators tackling environment, education, or healthcare, ,

Name: The Earth Prize
Description: The Earth Prize is a $100,000+ environmental sustainability competition open to teenage students worldwide. It recognizes and awards students who develop the best solutions to accelerate positive change towards environmental sustainability.
Evaluation_Criteria: Environmental scalability, ecological viability, freshness of approach, roadmap, Eco-innovator developing scalable hardware, biological, or behavioral climate solutions, ,

Name: International Young Eco-Hero Awards
Description:
The International Young Eco-Hero Awards are hosted annually by Action For Nature, a U.S.-based non-profit organization. Since 2003, the program has recognized and rewarded global youth environmental activists aged 8 to 16 who design and execute creative projects targeting the world's most critical environmental challenges.
The evaluation panels consist of experts in biology, environmental science, and education. Selected eco-heroes receive a cash prize of up to $1,000, an achievement certificate, public and media recognition, and exclusive access to the global Eco-Hero Alumni network.
Evaluation_Criteria: Independent initiative, measurable environmental improvement, educational outreach, Young climate activist or scientist who initiated and brought to fruition an independent eco-project, ,

Name: picoCTF (Carnegie Mellon)
Description: CyLab Security Academy is Carnegie Mellon University’s free cybersecurity learning platform. From foundational security concepts to cutting-edge topics like AI security and blockchain integrity, everything you need to learn, compete, and grow is right here. Same team, new mission.
Evaluation_Criteria: Reverse engineering, web exploitation, cryptography, binary exploitation, Curious security researcher capable of discovering and exploiting software logic flaws, ,

Name: CyberPatriot National Youth Cyber Defense
Description:
CyberPatriot is the world’s largest National Youth Cyber Education Program, propelling K-12 students toward careers in cybersecurity and other STEM disciplines, including the National Youth Cyber Defense Competition.
It puts teams of high school and middle school students in the position of newly hired IT professionals tasked with managing the network of a small company. Through a series of online competition rounds, teams are given a set of virtual operating systems and are tasked with finding and fixing cybersecurity vulnerabilities while maintaining critical services.  The top teams in the nation earn all-expenses-paid trips to Maryland for the National Finals Competition where they can earn national recognition and scholarship money.
Evaluation_Criteria: System hardening, vulnerability detection, adherence to OS security benchmarks, Methodical cybersecurity team proficient in auditing operating systems and terminal scripting, ,

Name: World Robotics Olympiad (WRO)
Description: The World Robot Olympiad (WRO) is a global stage where students harness the rapidly evolving power of robotics to tackle real-world problems. For the 2026 challenge, we urge participants to look beyond purely technical applications and consider how robotics can become a vital tool to express, preserve, and share the unique heritage, arts, and human stories that form the very foundation of global culture and identity.
Evaluation_Criteria: Autonomous task completion, sensor accuracy, mechanical economy, adaptability, Precision robotics builder comfortable programming sensors, motors, and linkages for edge cases, ,

Name: European Union Contest for Young Scientists (EUCYS)
Description: The EU Contest for Young Scientists (EUCYS) is an annual science competition initiated by the European Commission in 1989 to promote research cooperation and exchange among secondary school and university students. The European Union (EU) Contest for Young Scientists is a science fair, initiated by the European Commission. It is a part of the European Union Framework Programmes for Research and Technological Development, and is managed by the Directorate General for Research in the European Commission.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific originality, research standard, clear methodology, lucid oral defense, Winner of a primary national science competition presenting deep research across sciences, ,

Name: Stockholm Junior Water Prize
Description: The Stockholm Junior Water Prize (SJWP) is the world's most prestigious international competition for high school students (ages 15–20) addressing water-related environmental, scientific, social, and technological challenges. Beginning in 1995, the award is given annually for an outstanding water project by a young person or a small group of young people at a ceremony held during the World Water Week in Stockholm. The first two years the competition was held on a national level in Sweden. From 1997[1] onward the competition has been held in its current international format. The international Stockholm Junior Water Prize winner receives a US$15,000 scholarship and a blue crystal sculpture.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific relevance, methodology, research quality, practical feasibility, Dedicated young scientist targeting water purification, aquatic ecology, or hydrological crises, ,

Name: Blue Ocean Student Entrepreneur Competition
Description:
The Blue Ocean Student Entrepreneur Competition is the largest and most prestigious virtual business competition for high school students in the world.
The competition gives high school students the chance to present their innovative business ideas, hone their pitching skills, earn cash prizes, and build resumes that stand out from the crowd when applying for college. Most of all they learn how to create businesses that stand out from the competition, creating blue oceans of new market space.
The Blue Ocean Student Entrepreneur Competition was founded in Maryland in 2014 by a young budding high school entrepreneur directly inspired by Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne’s Blue Ocean Strategy and the blue ocean way of thinking.
Evaluation_Criteria: Elimination of trade-offs, uncontested market whitespace, value curves, pitch delivery, Forward-thinking business strategist able to identify oversaturated industries and carve out demand, ,

Name: Veer Gatha Project
Description: The Veer Gatha Project is a joint initiative launched by the Ministry of Defence (MoD) and the Ministry of Education (MoE) under the Gallantry Awards Portal to inspire school students and spread awareness about the acts of bravery of India's Gallantry Award winners and historical warriors.
Evaluation_Criteria: Expressive tribute, historical accuracy, emotional sincerity, artistic composition, Creative Indian student demonstrating strong command over patriotic prose, poetry, or art, ,

Name: CSIR Innovation Award for School Children
Description: The CSIR Innovation Award for School Children (CIASC) is a national annual competition launched in 2002 by the Council of Scientific & Industrial Research on World Intellectual Property Day (26th April) to foster scientific curiosity, creativity, and intellectual property (IP) awareness among young students.
Evaluation_Criteria: Technological novelty, industrial utility, commercial feasibility, patentability, Young Indian inventor creating functional low-cost solutions to real-world industrial roadblocks, ,

Name: Young Investors Society Stock Pitch
Description: The Young Investors Society (YIS) Global Stock Pitch Competition is an international financial analysis and public-speaking competition where high school students (competing individually or in teams of up to two) research a publicly traded company, build an investment thesis, and defend a Buy, Sell, or Hold recommendation before a panel of industry professionals and university professors.
Evaluation_Criteria: DCF valuation precision, thesis durability, competitive advantage analysis, Finance enthusiast capable of reading 10-Ks, modeling cash flows, and pitching equity, ,

Name: Ayn Rand Institute Essay Contests
Description: The Ayn Rand Institute (ARI) Essay Contests are annual international writing competitions that invite students worldwide to engage with the philosophical themes of Ayn Rand's classic novels: Anthem, The Fountainhead, and Atlas Shrugged. Having awarded over $2.2 million in cash prizes to more than 11,000 students since launching in 1985, the contests are completely free to enter and open to middle school, high school, college, and graduate students.
Evaluation_Criteria: Textual command, integration of Objectivist philosophical themes, clarity, Analytic reader able to synthesize literary motifs with individualist moral philosophy, ,

Name: Berkeley Economic Review High School Contest
Description: The Berkeley Economic Review High School Essay Contest invites high school students to explore economic topics through essay writing. For Spring 2026, contestants choose one of two prompts: (1) the economics of artificial intelligence, examining how AI adoption reshapes labor demand across skill levels and affects wage inequality, with a proposed policy response; or (2) education and the rising cost of college as a contributor to income inequality. Essays must be supported by evidence from credible sources and include a works cited page. Use of AI writing tools is not permitted. Winning essays will be published in the Berkeley Economic Review magazine, Equilibrium, and featured on the organization's website and social media.
Evaluation_Criteria: Empirical economic argumentation, clear thesis, data citation, policy relevance, Budding economist who can produce clean 750-word persuasive op-eds rooted in economics, ,

Name: Columbia Undergraduate Law Review Contest
Description: The Columbia Undergraduate Law Review (CULR) High School Essay Contest is an annual global remote essay competition for high school students. This contest was launched in collaboration with in partnership with the Equal Rights Amendment (ERA) Project at Columbia Law School, advised by Katherine Franke, James L. Dohr Professor of Law at Columbia Law School, and Ting Ting Cheng, civil rights attorney and Director of the ERA Project.
Evaluation_Criteria: Legal precedent interpretation, statutory reasoning, argumentative structure, Pre-law scholar with a talent for dissecting Supreme Court jurisprudence and legal policy, ,

Name: Trinity College Cambridge R.A. Butler Politics Prize
Description:
The R.A. Butler Politics Prize is an annual essay competition in politics and international studies jointly organized by Trinity College Cambridge and the University of Cambridge's Department of Politics and International Studies (POLIS). The objectives of the R.A. Butler Prize are twofold. Firstly, it aims to encourage students with an interest in modern politics and world affairs to think about undertaking university studies in Politics, International Studies or a related discipline; it is not limited to those already studying these subjects or indeed other social sciences. Secondly, its intention is to recognise the achievements both of high-calibre students and of those who teach them.
Essays can be up to 3,000 words, including all footnotes and references but excluding the bibliography.  It’s worth considering the use of examples in your essays: the best essays often use a diverse selection of contemporary, historical or literary examples.  We encourage you to provide references to your sources of information, and to include a bibliography at the end of the essay.  There is no recommended referencing or bibliographic style – use whatever format you think works best.  Please include your name on the document and save the file as “Surname, First name”.
Evaluation_Criteria: Philosophical sophistication, critical scrutiny of political doctrine, prose economy, Humanities student preparing for competitive PPE or Law admissions with superior written logic

Name: Adroit Prizes for Poetry and Prose
Description: The Adroit Prizes for Poetry and Prose are annual literary awards presented by The Adroit Journal to honor exceptional writing by secondary school and undergraduate students worldwide.
Evaluation_Criteria: Stylistic innovation, voice command, non-formulaic narratives, poetic depth, Emerging creative writer publishing work capable of standing beside established literary figures, ,

Name: MIT PokerBots
Description:
6.9630, or MIT Pokerbots, is a computerized poker tournament. Teams have one month to program a completely autonomous pokerbot which competes against other bots in a unique poker variant. Competitors must learn and apply concepts in mathematics, computer science, and economics not normally developed together in academic settings in order to conquer their opponents and emerge victorious.
This year's competition features over $50,000 in prizes and attention from the most prestigious quantitative trading and technology firms. This IAP, channel your programming ability and strategic quantitative thinking skills to become the reigning Pokerbots champion!
Evaluation_Criteria: Game theory optimal play, counter-exploitation, risk management, execution speed, Quant-minded coder fluent in probability, game trees, and reinforcement algorithms, ,

Name: NASA International Space Apps Challenge
Description: The NASA International Space Apps Challenge is a global annual hackathon. This two-day event provides an opportunity for participants to utilize NASA's free and open data and its Space Agency Partners' space-based data to address real-world problems on Earth and in space.
Evaluation_Criteria: Utilization of NASA data sets, user accessibility, solution originality, space value, Space exploration enthusiast and collaborative coder eager to tackle Earth and space science, ,

Name: Bow Seat Ocean Awareness Contest
Description: The Bow Seat Blue Planet Awareness Contest (formerly the Ocean Awareness Contest) is an international youth art and advocacy competition. The 2027 Blue Planet Awareness Contest – Nature of Truth – challenges you to think critically about both natural and digital landscapes through the lens of environmental disinformation. Disinformation has long been used to generate discourse to delay or stop environmental action, and it has only been supercharged in today’s digital age. Be part of the solution and raise awareness about what environmental disinformation looks like through art, writing, performance, film, or multimedia.
Evaluation_Criteria: Intersectional eco-storytelling, emotional resonance, creative risk, research depth, Youth climate communicator weaving scientific facts into poignant stories, poetry, or art

Name: MIT Solve
Description: MIT Solve is an initiative of the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) founded in 2016 that acts as a marketplace for social impact innovation. It uses open innovation and crowdsourcing to find early-stage, technology-driven entrepreneurs and social innovators from around the world who are addressing critical global challenges. The MIT Solve Open Challenges provide hundreds of thousands of dollars in funding, as well as mentorship.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scalability, human-centered design, operational feasibility, community partnership, Social entrepreneurs with scalable tech prototypes directly tackling UN Sustainable Development Goals, ,

Name: India AI Impact Festival
Description: The India AI Impact Festival 2026 is a national innovation platform organized collaboratively by MeitY, INDIAai, STPI, NIELIT, AIM (NITI Aayog), and Intel India to showcase inclusive artificial intelligence solutions built for Bharat.
Evaluation_Criteria: Ethical AI usage, indigenous problem-solving, algorithmic feasibility, public impact, Indian students developing applied computer vision or NLP solutions for regional social upliftment, ,

Name: Microsoft Imagine Cup Junior
Description: Microsoft Imagine Cup Junior is a global youth program and design-thinking challenge that introduces students to artificial intelligence (AI) and technology for social good. It is not a software-coding contest. Instead, it focuses on design thinking, teaching students to brainstorm and pitch concepts that solve real-world problems using AI.
Evaluation_Criteria: AI for Good alignment, conceptual understanding, design thinking, presentation deck, Young students exploring how AI can solve accessibility, environmental, and health challenges, ,

Name: HPE CodeWars
Description: HPE CodeWars is an annual international computer programming competition hosted by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) for high school and school students.
Evaluation_Criteria: Speed of algorithmic execution, test-case coverage, team problem-solving strategy, Versatile high school coders comfortable racing against the clock in Python, Java, or C++,

Name: HPE Code Battle
Description: HPE Code Battle, hosted by Hewlett Packard Enterprise in collaboration with Codingal, is an annual international computer programming competition for high school and school students.
Evaluation_Criteria: Algorithmic optimization, computational speed, dynamic programming competence, Competitive programmers adept at rapid-fire problem solving under strict runtime bounds, ,

Name: Columbia Junior Science Journal
Description: The Columbia Junior Science Journal (CJSJ) is a highly selective high school research journal seeking original research papers and review articles. We provide high school students with a platform to publish manuscripts in the fields of natural sciences, physical sciences, engineering, and social sciences. Selected CJSJ authors demonstrate the ability to communicate research projects to the general public and scientific community. CJSJ promotes the development of young researchers versed in technical and communication skills, which are facets encoded into the DNA of Columbia University.
Evaluation_Criteria: Methodological rigor, clarity of scientific communication, experimental reproducibility, Young scientific researcher with a completed research project seeking formal academic validation, ,

Name: AI Tinkerpreneur
Description:
The India AI Tinkerpreneur, organized by Atal Innovation Mission (AIM), NITI Aayog in collaboration with Intel, is a series of 25 AI-skilling workshops with AI as an overarching theme, featuring domain-specific sessions by eminent speakers, culminating with a final competition where students submit there AI innovations along with business plans. 
It is a national launchpad to empower young minds with the mindset, skillsets, and the confidence to innovate and create ATL and AI-enabled projects to address social issues.
Evaluation_Criteria: Digital prototype completion, business canvas clarity, digital marketing execution, Indian ATL lab innovators eager to translate hardware/software experiments into products, ,

Name: Young Innovator's Programme IITKGP
Description: The Young Innovators' Program (YIP) is a flagship annual competition hosted by the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur to foster scientific curiosity, creativity, and problem-solving skills among school students. Top teams nationwide will be selected after the first round and they will be called to Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur to exhibit and demonstrate their models or prototype and charts which will be evaluated by professors of IIT Kharagpur.
Evaluation_Criteria: Novelty of concept, scientific foundation, industrial feasibility, live demonstration, Science and engineering enthusiasts with practical working prototypes addressing real challenges, ,

Name: World Bank Youth Summit
Description:
The World Bank Group Youth Summit Pitch Competition is a global opportunity for young innovators and entrepreneurs to showcase bold, impactful solutions to today’s most pressing development challenges.
Open to individuals and teams aged 18–35 from around the world, this flagship initiative offers a unique platform to present ideas to an international audience and accelerate the journey from concept to impact.
Evaluation_Criteria: Developmental impact, economic sustainability, financial viability, scalability, Young economists and social leaders designing policy or enterprise frameworks for developing nations

Name: Eureka! Jr. IIT Bombay
Description: Eureka! Junior is a national-level business model and entrepreneurship competition for school students in Classes 6 to 12, organized by the Entrepreneurship Cell (E-Cell) of IIT Bombay.
Evaluation_Criteria: Business feasibility, market validation, financial sustainability, pitch quality, Aspiring Indian teen entrepreneurs seeking institutional seed support and entrepreneurship mentoring, ,

Name: IBM Call for Code
Description: The Call For Code AI initiative—founded by David Clark Cause with founding partner IBM, global impact partner UN Human Rights, and open source partner the Linux Foundation—unites over 1 million developers across 190+ countries to build responsible, open-source AI solutions addressing global challenges.
Evaluation_Criteria: Code quality, integration of IBM Cloud/open-source tools, climate relevance, Full-stack developers and AI practitioners building production-ready climate mitigation software

Name: Crimson 18u18
Description: Crimson 18u18 is a global initiative by Crimson Education that annually recognizes 18 exceptional changemakers under the age of 18. The program spotlights high-achieving teens who demonstrate significant community impact, innovation, leadership, and talent across multiple fields.
Evaluation_Criteria: Demonstrated leadership, exceptional agency, quantifiable initiative outcomes, High-achieving self-starter with a standout extracurricular portfolio and community footprint

Name: NYAS Junior Academy
Description: The Junior Academy is a project-based learning program where students form international teams and work with STEM experts through an online community platform. Students participate in Innovation Challenges where they collaborate under the guidance of STEM mentors to design solutions to real-world problems. Students and mentors can participate from anywhere in the world.
Evaluation_Criteria: Collaborative teamwork, application of scientific method, design thinking, Curious, collaborative STEM student passionate about international multidisciplinary problem solving, ,

Name: Mercedes-Benz Fellowship
Description: beVisioneers: The Mercedes-Benz Fellowship is a global, fully funded 2-year hybrid fellowship designed for young eco-innovators aged 18 to 28 who are building planet-positive and environmental projects. Implemented by The DO School and primarily funded through Mercedes-Benz donations (stemming from the historic 2022 auction of the 1955 Mercedes-Benz 300 SLR Uhlenhaut Coupé), the program supports roughly 250 innovators annually across impact areas like clean energy, circular economy, waste reduction, and sustainable mobility.
Evaluation_Criteria: Leadership potential, project scalability, social cohesion impact, commitment, Visionary civic leader running an active community enterprise centered on sustainable development, ,

Name: Microsoft Imagine Cup
Description: The Microsoft Imagine Cup is Microsoft's premier global student tech and startup competition where student founders build AI-powered solutions using Azure and Microsoft cloud technologies.
Evaluation_Criteria: Azure tech architecture, market viability, startup traction, business model, Technical founder team building an enterprise-grade AI or cloud startup on Microsoft stack, ,

Name: Harvard Crimson Global Case Competition
Description: The Harvard Crimson Global Case Competition (HCGCC) is a premier virtual international business strategy and consulting competition for high school students aged 13–18, co-hosted online by The Harvard Crimson and Crimson Education. Participants step into the shoes of CEOs and management consultants to solve real-world corporate challenges.
Evaluation_Criteria: Strategic problem breakdown, financial modeling, presentation polish, Q&A defense, Analytical thinker adept at business strategy, PowerPoint presentations, and corporate analysis, ,

Name: Leading Minds Fellowship - UNICEF
Description:
The Climate Education Fellowship is a youth-led, youth-centered initiative designed to strengthen the global understanding of what works in climate education. The Fellowship focuses on building a robust evidence base through youth-driven research, foresight, and strategic convening.  
UNICEF is selecting up to 12 young climate leaders (ages 10–30) who are strengthening climate education in their schools, communities, and countries in both formal and informal settings.  
These Leading Minds Climate Education Fellows will join a global cohort shaping policy, elevating youth-led initiatives, and helping design strategic convenings.
Evaluation_Criteria: Grassroots advocacy record, lived experience perspectives, public communication, Empathetic youth advocate with an established voice in mental health or child rights reform, ,

Name: CREST Awards (British Council)
Description: CREST Awards are hands-on, student-led STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Math) project schemes for young people aged 3 to 19, run by the British Science Association (not the British Council).
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific inquiry process, project independence, safety compliance, reporting, Student conducting thorough, self-directed research or engineering design experiments

Name: EarthEcho International Youth Leadership Council
Description:
EarthEcho International was founded on the belief that young people have the power to change the world. You are invited to apply to join the Youth Leadership Council (YLC) - a team of young environmental leaders, selected annually through a competitive application process, who play a key role leading EarthEcho’s programs while developing and implementing campaigns to mobilize young people worldwide to protect our ocean planet.
Through this unique experience, you will grow as an environmental leader, gain an understanding of the operations of an international non-profit organization as you shape our work and mission, and build connections with your peers and EarthEcho partners working around the world to ensure a sustainable future.
Evaluation_Criteria: Environmental track record, youth mobilization capacity, collaborative mindset, Passionate marine or environmental activist with hands-on conservation and campaigning experience, ,

Name: Stanford Climate Leaders Fellowship
Description: The Climate Leaders Fellowship, a collaboration between the Stanford University Deliberative Democracy Lab, the Rustic Pathways Foundation and Rustic Pathways, is a transformative program connecting passionate high school students worldwide to address climate change. Through research, planning, and community projects, fellows develop leadership, organization, and communication skills, making a positive impact on local issues while learning from a global network of peers and advisors.
Evaluation_Criteria: Project execution, measurable local climate impact, peer collaboration, Student organizer dedicated to completing a structured 10-week community decarbonization project, ,

Name: Canterbury Tales Writing Competition
Description: The Canterbury Tales Writing Competition is a free global contest hosted by The Chaucer Heritage Trust for school-age students up to 18. The themed prompt challenges writers to explore poems, stories, or character descriptions based on a specific creative concept. Divided into junior, intermediate, and senior age groups, entries must be under 500 words. Winning entrants can receive up to £300 for themselves and £1,000 for their school or library, making it an excellent opportunity to showcase creative writing skills.
Evaluation_Criteria: Chaucerian adaptation, command of meter, narrative wit, characterization, Creative writer skilled in classical verse, medieval storytelling, and historical adaptation, ,

Name: MITES (MIT Introduction to Technology, Eng & Sci)
Description: MITES (MIT Introduction to Technology, Engineering, and Science) is a prestigious, tuition-free pre-college STEM program run by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). It's a rigorous, 6-week residential experience on MIT’s campus in Cambridge, Massachusetts, for rising high school seniors. Students take 5 college-level courses in math, life sciences, physics, humanities, and engineering, alongside hands-on projects and symposia.
Evaluation_Criteria: Academic excellence in math/science, socio-economic context, STEM passion, High-achieving junior with top grades and passion for quantitative engineering careers,

Name: World Science Scholars
Description: World Science Scholars is a free, global online program for over 400 extraordinarily gifted high school and accelerated middle school students across 50 countries. Co-founded by physicist Brian Greene and Tracy Day as an initiative of the World Science Festival, the program connects young minds with Nobel laureates, visionary thinkers, and leading scientists.
Evaluation_Criteria: Mathematical aptitude, theoretical reasoning, intellectual curiosity, Prodigious mathematical mind capable of digesting tensor calculus, quantum theory, and relativity, ,

Name: 1M1B Future Leaders (One Million Leaders)
Description: 1M1B (One Million for One Billion) is a United Nations-accredited nonprofit organization established in 2014, founded by Manav Subodh. The organization focuses on digital skilling, change-making, and entrepreneurship, aiming to equip youth throughout India with essential skills such as artificial Intelligence (AI), Green Skills, Entrepreneurship, Digital Citizenship, Augmented Reality (AR), Virtual Reality (VR), and other emerging technologies. The Future Leaders program is a comprehensive leadership development initiative that aims to create a new generation of socially conscious leaders who can tackle societal issues in a sustainable manner. As a part of this program, 14 students from Bengaluru were shortlisted to present their impact projects at the UN Headquarters in New York. 14-year-old Divaa Uthkarsha, who won the Diana Award in 2023 for her humanitarian project, Project Surya, was mentored by 1M1B through the Future Leaders programme.
Evaluation_Criteria: Measurable social impact, alignment with UN SDGs, community engagement, Active Indian student seeking structured mentorship to launch and scale a local community campaign, ,

Name: Northeastern University London Essay Competition
Description: The Northeastern University London Essay Competition (frequently cross-hosted or run alongside platforms like Minds Underground) is a prestigious international academic writing competition. It is explicitly designed for students in their penultimate year of secondary education (Year 12 in the UK, Grade 11 in India, or international equivalent). The university has recently diversified this track into the immersive online AI Futures Challenge, focusing heavily on technological innovation alongside traditional humanities and social sciences.
Evaluation_Criteria: Argumentative coherence, critical nuance, scholarly citation, voice
Ideal_Candidate: Prospective undergraduate humanities student preparing analytical essays for university entrance

Name: Oxford Royale Essay Competition
Description:
Academy Royale International is a leading provider of academic summer schools for students aged 12 to 18. Participants can choose to study from one of 14 subjects across a range of disciplines – from Law and Medicine, to Engineering and Film – on campus at leading universities in the UK.
Each year, they host an academic essay competition for ambitious students across the world, aged from 12 to 18. Students can select from a range of pre-defined essay topics, which are split into two categories: ages 12 to 15 and 16 to 18. You can find the full details of these topics below.
Evaluation_Criteria: Intellectual passion, originality of thought, persuasive structure, Ambitious student seeking fully funded residential summer study at Oxford or Cambridge, ,

Name: Open Letters: Opinion-Writing Contest (New York Times)
Description: The Open Letters: Opinion-Writing Contest is an annual student writing competition hosted by The New York Times Learning Network. The challenge is to write an open letter of 500 words or fewer to a specific audience or person in power, calling attention to an issue and prompting action or reflection.
Evaluation_Criteria: Persuasive clarity, rhetorical device usage, emotional and evidence balance, Young essayist capable of addressing a specific public figure or institution with persuasive force, ,

Name: Hack3
Description: Hack3 is a 24-hour global event where students "hack" together solutions to today's most pressing problems, network with other students, attend workshops, and receive feedback from judges. All 100% free.
Evaluation_Criteria: Project completeness, ease of use, code design, beginner effort, Beginner to intermediate student developer seeking their first competitive project experience, ,

Name: HackNYU
Description: HackNYU is New York University’s premier student-run annual global hackathon, founded in 2010 and organized across NYU's global campuses (including New York, Abu Dhabi, and Shanghai).
Evaluation_Criteria: Technical sophistication, design UX, theme relevance, live presentation, Collaborative hacker wanting to build prototypes across Education, Sustainability, or Healthcare, ,

Name: Stanford ACM ProCo
Description: ProCo is a computer programming contest for high school students in the style of the college-level ACM-ICPC. ProCo aims to provide a fun and engaging opportunity for high school students in the Bay Area to explore their passion in computer science.
Evaluation_Criteria: Speed, correctness, algorithmic efficiency across ACM-ICPC style questions, Skilled high school algorithmic programmer adept at team synchronization under intense time bounds, ,

Name: TechXcelerate (BITS Pilani)
Description: TechXcelerate is a premier national-level hackathon, tech innovation, and internship event hosted at BITS Pilani campuses (such as the Hyderabad Campus and Goa Campus), as well as a related high-level virtual high school hackathon.
Evaluation_Criteria: Hardware prototype functionality, industrial design, presentation, Technical builder comfortable demonstrating physical IoT, robotics, or embedded systems, ,

Name: Mountain Hacks
Description: MountainHacks is the Tri-Valley area's largest hackathon, bringing students from around California to learn about technologies, innovative projects, and sharing with community.
Evaluation_Criteria: Creativity, functional completeness, presentation clarity, High school programmer testing new web frameworks or mobile tools with peers, ,

Name: HS Hacks
Description:
HS Hacks is a student-led hackathon designed specifically for high school students who want to explore the world of technology and innovation. Work together to use your creativity and problem-solving skills to develop innovative solutions!
This hackathon is beginner-friendly, and participants with any level of coding experience are welcome. The theme is here to inspire your ideas, and you are free to explore any aspect of technology and innovation that interests you. So come join us, bring your passion, and let's build our favorite hacks!
Evaluation_Criteria: Project utility, code cleanliness, user interface design, Collaborative student hacker creating functional applications over a 24-hour sprint, ,

Name: HackPoly
Description: Hackopoly is designed as a tech carnival-style game where participants earn HackCoins by solving challenges and can “buy” properties, unlock lifelines, or pay penalties—just like in Monopoly. It blends technology, creativity, and strategy into an engaging competition for all skill levels.
Evaluation_Criteria: Technical depth, engineering design, scalability, practical utility, Engineering-focused coder building hardware-software integrated prototypes, ,

Name: Stanford TreeHacks
Description:
TreeHacks is Stanford's premier hackathon. We fly out the world's most talented builders to Stanford, where they create products that tackle humanity's toughest challenges in just 36 hours.
Our hackers have food and travel covered, and get to compete for incredible prizes while networking with recruiters from top companies.
If you want to bring your ideas to life, even if you've never attented a hackathon, come to TreeHacks!
Evaluation_Criteria: Innovation, technical ambition, system architecture, social benefit, Elite high school software/hardware builder capable of competing with top university developers, ,

Name: NASA App Development Challenge
Description: The annual NASA Space Apps Challenge provides the opportunity to engage directly with NASA’s data, along with Space Agency Partner data. During the two-day hackathon, teams use this data to address challenges written by NASA Subject Matter Experts, featuring topics including storytelling, software development, astrophysics, space exploration, agriculture, and more.
Evaluation_Criteria: 3D visualization accuracy, trajectory math, UI cleanliness, video presentation, Student team with strong mathematical rendering and game engine (Unity/Unreal) coding skills, ,

Name: Hack Club Horizons
Description: Hack Club is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit and network of 60k+ technical high schoolers. We believe you learn best by building so we're creating community and providing grants so you can make awesome projects. Hack Club Horizons is a series of free, weekend-long coding hackathons and social coding marathons for teenagers (ages 13-18).
Evaluation_Criteria: Technical execution, open-source documentation, ship velocity, Scrappy, self-motivated hacker who loves open-source programming, soldering, and shipping code, ,

Name: CodeDay Labs
Description: CodeDay Labs is a 100% online, unpaid virtual technology internship program designed to match high school and college students with industry mentors and peers. Operated by the 501(c)(3) non-profit organization CodeDay (originally founded in 2009 as Student Research and Development), the program focuses on making tech careers accessible to underrepresented and underserved students.
Evaluation_Criteria: Foundational coding competency, teamwork, commitment to learn, Beginner to intermediate programmer wanting real-world software engineering experience, ,

Name: JAMHacks
Description: JAMHacks is Canada's largest high school hackathon, hosted annually in Waterloo, Ontario, with support from the University of Waterloo (Waterloo Engineering) and partners like Major League Hacking.
Evaluation_Criteria: Technical difficulty, UI aesthetic, problem originality, demo clarity, Creative Canadian or international student maker building full-stack web or hardware hacks, ,

Name: Los Altos Hacks
Description: Los Altos Hacks is the world's largest annual high school hackathon, bringing together hundreds of students ages 13–19 for beginner-friendly, 24-hour open-ended coding and hardware projects.
Evaluation_Criteria: Technical execution, originality, presentation polish, Bay Area or remote teen developer eager to interface with Silicon Valley mentors and APIs, ,

Name: Cornell High School Programming Contest
Description: The Cornell High School Programming Contest is an annual coding competition hosted collaboratively by the Cornell Bowers CIS (Computing and Information Science) and Cornell Tech.
Evaluation_Criteria: Algorithmic mastery, runtime efficiency, problem-solving speed, High-school competitive programming team trained in dynamic programming and graph theory, ,

Name: Bebras Computing Challenge
Description: The Bebras Computing Challenge is an international initiative that promotes informatics, computer science, and computational thinking among school students aged 6 to 19. Founded in 2004 in Lithuania by Prof. Valentina Dagienė, the name comes from bebras, the Lithuanian word for "beaver". Beavers were chosen to represent teamwork, intelligence, and persistence. The challenge tests logical problem-solving rather than programming syntax. It focuses on core computational skills like task decomposition, pattern recognition, abstraction, and algorithmic design.
Evaluation_Criteria: Computational logic, pattern recognition, algorithmic deduction, Young student testing logical problem-solving aptitude before diving into syntax-based programming, ,

Name: Canadian Computing Olympiad (CCO)
Description: The Canadian Computing Olympiad (CCO) is an exclusive, invitation-only programming contest organized annually by the University of Waterloo. It serves as the second stage of the Canadian Computing Competition (CCC) and acts as the qualifier to select Canada's teams for the International Olympiad in Informatics (IOI) and European Girls' Olympiad in Informatics (EGOI).
Evaluation_Criteria: Advanced algorithm design, data structure optimization, correctness under memory bounds, Elite competitive programmer aiming for national team selection and IOI medals, ,

Name: NYU Tandon CSAW High School CTF
Description: The NYU Tandon CSAW (Cyber Security Awareness Week) is the world’s largest student-run cybersecurity event, hosted across global academic centers including NYU Tandon, IIT Kanpur, NYU Abu Dhabi, Universidad Iberoamericana, and Grenoble INP - Esisar. CSAW historically features specialized tracks and challenges for high school students—such as forensics, cryptography, reverse engineering, and red team/infiltration scenarios (like investigating fictional companies or embedded systems). Regional variants like CSAW Europe also run a dedicated Red Team Competition for high schoolers.
Evaluation_Criteria: Binary exploitation, reverse engineering, cryptography, forensic analysis, Team of aspiring white-hat hackers who spend time dissecting binaries and web exploits, ,

Name: Teens in AI - Global AI Hackathon
Description: The Global AI Techathon (also known as the Teens in AI Global Hackathon) is a free, annual hybrid and virtual learning challenge organized by Teens in AI. The core focus is on building artificial intelligence and data science solutions for social good, specifically targeting the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) (such as health, education, gender equality, and reduced inequalities).
Evaluation_Criteria: AI ethics, SDG alignment, machine learning feasibility, business pitch, Ethically conscious teen eager to explore introductory AI models to solve civic dilemmas, ,

Name: Xylem Global Student Innovation Challenge
Description:
Water is essential to healthy communities, thriving economies, and a sustainable future. Yet growing demand, pollution, aging infrastructure, climate change, and unequal access continue to put pressure on water resources around the world.
The Xylem Global Student Innovation Challenge 2026 is your chance to tackle these critical issues head-on. Over eight weeks, students ages 13-25 from around the world will team up, get creative, and build solutions that make a real impact.
Evaluation_Criteria: Feasibility, hydrological problem-solving, technological creativity, Youth innovator focused on environmental technology and data-driven sustainability solutions, ,

Name: Games for Change (G4C) Student Challenge
Description: A G4C Student Challenge Game Jam is a fun, hands-on learning experience where students design and prototype games inspired by real-world challenges. As part of the G4C Student Challenge, it introduces young people to game design while encouraging them to explore social impact and problem-solving through projects they can submit to the Student Challenge competition.
Evaluation_Criteria: Game mechanics, thematic storytelling, visual design, player engagement, Aspiring indie game developer or digital artist combining coding with civic storytelling, ,

Name: Hack Club Paradox
Description:
Hack Club Paradox is a YSWS ("You Ship, We Ship") program or challenge run by Hack Club. You build and ship projects that feature or revolve around a story, earning tickets along the way.
The Rewards: You can use your earned tickets to buy gear and swag from the Hack Club shop, or log 30 hours to qualify for Fable, an IRL (in-real-life) Hackathon in London, UK (scheduled around August 3–6, 2026).
Evaluation_Criteria: Hands-on technical curiosity, persistence, open-source spirit, Maker who loves building physical electronics, mechanical gadgets, or playful web experiments, ,

Name: VEX AI Competition
Description:
VEX AI, VEX GPS, and VEX LINK, and the resulting Sensor Fusion create an opportunity for students to take their autonomous robots a level up! The VEX AI Competition pushes the boundaries of robotics competitions. 
The game is separate from the VRC and VEX U competitions.Each team brings two robots that they design and build to work as a team. Teams can 3D print and machine parts. Teams can use custom electronics, and there are no motor quantity limits. This game will be open to Secondary School students and University students alike.
Evaluation_Criteria: Computer vision accuracy, sensor fusion, autonomous path planning, mechanical build, Advanced robotics programmer comfortable working with OpenCV, ROS, and autonomous motion

Name: Botball Educational Robotics Program
Description: Autonomous robotics program utilizing AI and computer vision on embedded Linux controllers without remotes.
Evaluation_Criteria: Autonomous C code, mechanical engineering, sensor integration, documentation, Engineering student who enjoys programming autonomous robotic arms, pathing, and gear trains, ,

Name: Robofest
Description: Autonomous STEM robotics competition hosted by Lawrence Technological University focusing on math.
Evaluation_Criteria: Autonomous problem execution, algorithmic precision, mathematical formulation, Student builder who prefers pure autonomous algorithmic challenges over remote-controlled games, ,

Name: School Enterprise Challenge
Description: Global educational program supporting students to set up and run real, profitable businesses in school.
Evaluation_Criteria: Real business revenue, sustainability, educational impact, teamwork, School-based team wanting to start an on-campus business that generates actual profits,

Name: The Create Apps Championship
Description: Youth app development competition focused on functional mobile creations using visual or syntax code.
Evaluation_Criteria: App UI design, code logic, problem-solving utility, App creator building functional mobile prototypes in MIT App Inventor, Flutter, or React Native, ,

Name: Global Innovation Challenge
Description: Student challenge inviting novel hardware and software concepts targeting UN global development goals.
Evaluation_Criteria: Originality of concept, societal need, engineering feasibility, Cross-disciplinary student team formulating technical answers to systemic global crises, ,

Name: Inflection Grants
Description: Fast funding grants awarded to young individuals working on breakthroughs in math, AI, and science.
Evaluation_Criteria: Individual agency, intellectual clarity, asymmetric upside of project, Unorthodox young researcher or builder tackling high-risk, high-reward technical projects

Name: NFTE World Series of Innovation
Description: Challenge series inviting youth to solve global challenges focused on the UN Sustainable Development Goals.
Evaluation_Criteria: Business model viability, SDG alignment, customer empathy, pitch presentation, Enterprising teen who can quickly package a creative idea into a cohesive business proposition, ,

Name: GENIUS Olympiad
Description: International high school project competition focused on environmental issues across science, writing, and art.
Evaluation_Criteria: Environmental focus, scientific rigor, poster design, oral presentation, Eco-minded student researcher presenting environmental science experiments or design solutions

Name: SAGE Global Competition
Description: Global teen entrepreneurship competition emphasizing socially responsible business ventures.
Evaluation_Criteria: Financial sustainability, social impact, ethical stewardship, oral presentation, Teen entrepreneur whose business generates measurable revenue while improving community welfare, ,

Name: Youth Citizen Entrepreneurship Competition
Description: Global program supporting young changemakers rolling out innovative ideas with measurable community impact.
Evaluation_Criteria: Innovative thinking, community engagement, entrepreneurial design, Grassroots youth leader passionate about building sustainable civic community projects, ,

Name: Astro Pi Challenge (ESA)
Description: Program giving young coders the chance to run their Python code aboard the International Space Station.
Evaluation_Criteria: Sensor data collection logic, Python code safety, scientific hypothesis, Young space enthusiast eager to write real Python experiments executed in orbital microgravity, ,

Name: RoboCupJunior
Description: International robotics competition emphasizing autonomous robots competing in Soccer, Rescue, and OnStage.
Evaluation_Criteria: Autonomous robotics software, mechanical design, dynamic obstacle avoidance, Robotics programmer capable of tuning multi-sensor autonomous systems to track balls and lines

Name: Zero Robotics (MIT / NASA)
Description: Robotics tournament where students write C++ code to control autonomous satellites on the ISS.
Evaluation_Criteria: Path optimization, fuel efficiency, game strategy, mathematical collision avoidance, Student programmer interested in orbital mechanics, 3D coordinate math, and control algorithms, ,

Name: YUVAi: Global Youth Challenge
Description: National AI readiness initiative fostering deep understanding of AI concepts among Indian students.
Evaluation_Criteria: AI conceptual clarity, prototype utility, responsible AI implementation, Indian school coder developing practical AI applications to address regional community issues, ,

Name: Global Sustainability Challenge
Description: Youth innovation contest focusing on scalable, localized green technology and sustainable infrastructure.
Evaluation_Criteria: Ecological impact, economic feasibility, presentation clarity, Team of students eager to design sustainable alternatives for urban waste or energy systems,

Name: IB Global Youth Action Fund
Description: Grant program awarding up to $3000 to International Baccalaureate students leading social impact projects.
Evaluation_Criteria: Alignment with UN SDGs, project feasibility, financial management, community voice, IB Diploma student utilizing their CAS requirement to lead a measurable civic initiative, ,

Name: Amazon Web Services (AWS) DeepRacer League
Description: Global autonomous 1/18th scale car racing league using reinforcement learning models trained on AWS.
Evaluation_Criteria: Reward function design, model convergence, lap time, reinforcement efficiency, Student coder eager to learn reinforcement learning and hyperparameter tuning hands-on, ,

Name: Eurasia Young Scientist Exhibition (YSE) / CASTIC
Description: Premier Asian science and technology innovation contest welcoming international school researchers.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific innovation, practical utility, research documentation, International student researcher presenting original engineering or biological research findings, ,

Name: Breakthrough Junior Challenge
Description: Global science video competition where students explain a complex concept in physics, life sciences, or math.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific accuracy, creative presentation, engagement, communication clarity, Charismatic student communicator capable of turning complex theoretical math/physics into dynamic video

Name: Yau Science Awards (YMSA)
Description: Founded by Fields Medalist Shing-Tung Yau, evaluating university-level research in math and sciences.
Evaluation_Criteria: Mathematical rigor, academic depth, original theoretical insight, Prodigious math and science student capable of writing formal academic research monographs,

Name: International Conference of Young Scientists (ICYS)
Description: International arena for secondary school researchers defending scientific papers in physics and math.
Evaluation_Criteria: Methodological rigor, experimental data analysis, academic presentation defense, Dedicated student researcher capable of defending experimental methodology before international faculty, ,

Name: International Young Physicists' Tournament (IYPT)
Description: Physics World Cup where national student teams debate complex open-ended physical phenomena.
Evaluation_Criteria: Physical intuition, experimental reproducibility, oral defense, opposition critique, Sharp physics student who excels at open-ended experimental problem solving and technical debate, ,

Name: London International Youth Science Forum (LIYSF)
Description: Two-week residential science forum at Imperial College London hosting top young scientists.
Evaluation_Criteria: Academic excellence, passion for applied science, global perspective, Top science student seeking high-level lectures, laboratory tours, and international scientific networking, ,

Name: BioGENEius Global Challenge
Description: Premier high school biotechnology competition focusing on healthcare, agriculture, and environment.
Evaluation_Criteria: Biotech innovation, experimental design, potential industry application, Aspiring biological scientist conducting laboratory research with direct clinical or environmental utility

Name: International Sustainable World Project Olympiad (I-SWEEEP)
Description: International science fair focused on ground-breaking energy, engineering, and environmental solutions.
Evaluation_Criteria: Innovation, environmental relevance, scientific methodology, poster defense, Student environmental engineer who has created functional prototypes for renewable energy

Name: The Big Bang UK Young Scientists Competition
Description: The UK's largest annual celebration of STEM achievements for young people presenting original projects.
Evaluation_Criteria: STEM approach, project planning, communication, real-world relevance, UK school student with an inventive science or engineering project tested through experiments, ,

Name: The Singapore Science and Engineering Fair
Description: National science fair in Singapore selecting delegates for Regeneron ISEF and international showcases.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific approach, experimental thoroughness, technical understanding, Top Singaporean student researcher working with A*STAR or university research mentors, ,

Name: Initiative for Research and Innovation in STEM (IRIS)
Description: India's premier research fair directly affiliated with Regeneron ISEF selecting Team India.
Evaluation_Criteria: Novelty of research, scientific methodology, experimental data, oral presentation, Top student researcher in India who has conducted lab-verified original science experiments, ,

Name: Tidewater Science and Engineering Fair
Description: Regional ISEF-affiliated science competition in Virginia welcoming high-caliber research projects.
Evaluation_Criteria: Scientific method, poster clarity, student understanding of research area, Regional high school researcher aiming to qualify for state and international science competitions, ,

Name: BIEA International STEM Competition
Description: British International Education Association contest challenging students to engineer ecological solutions.
Evaluation_Criteria: Engineering design, ecological problem solving, report writing, presentation, Team of students eager to design technological solutions (drones, robotics) for wildlife conservation, ,

Name: EUROINVENT Creativity & Innovation
Description: European exhibition dedicated to inventors, showcasing patents and student research inventions.
Evaluation_Criteria: Novelty, industrial applicability, prototype execution, patent potential, Student inventor with a functional prototype or patent application seeking global exhibition,

Name: Imperial College Schools Science Competition
Description: Science communication contest tasking teams to film a 1-minute video answering a scientific question.
Evaluation_Criteria: Creativity, scientific accuracy, communication engagement, teamwork, Young science communicator capable of explaining real scientific solutions in an engaging video, ,

Name: IGNITE International Energy Transition Comp
Description: Youth challenge seeking technological and policy solutions accelerating the global shift to clean energy.
Evaluation_Criteria: Energy transition viability, engineering creativity, policy integration, Student team passionate about renewable power, battery storage, and climate economics, ,

Name: Fitzwilliam College Cambridge Economics Essay Prize
Description: Prestigious Cambridge college prize challenging students to critically evaluate contemporary economic prompts.
Evaluation_Criteria: Economic analysis, independent evaluation, persuasive clarity, scholarship, Ambitious high school economist preparing for rigorous Oxbridge undergraduate study, ,

Name: Fraser Institute Student Essay Contest
Description: Economics essay contest by Canada's leading public policy think tank on markets and policy.
Evaluation_Criteria: Understanding of market principles, empirical support, clarity of argumentation, Student interested in market economics, public finance, and Canadian/global policy evaluation, ,

Name: Gould Prize for Essays in English Literature
Description: Cambridge college essay prize hosted by Trinity College for critical essays in English literature.
Evaluation_Criteria: Literary insight, analytical independence, depth of reading, close textual scrutiny, Perceptive reader capable of sophisticated literary criticism and historical context analysis, ,

Name: High School Academic Research Comp (SARC)
Description: International competition providing high school researchers an evaluation platform for academic papers.
Evaluation_Criteria: Research methodology, academic paper structure, clarity of contribution, Secondary student who has completed an academic paper seeking review from university researchers, ,

Name: IEA Monetary Policy Essay Prize
Description: Essay competition hosted by the Institute of Economic Affairs focusing on monetary policy and inflation.
Evaluation_Criteria: Monetary economic theory, empirical data use, analytical clarity, Student studying economics with an interest in central banking, inflation, and interest rate policy, ,

Name: Jane Austen Society of North America (JASNA) Contest
Description: Literary essay competition exploring the novels, characters, and cultural themes of Jane Austen.
Evaluation_Criteria: Textual knowledge of Austen's works, analytical insight, graceful writing, Literature student who appreciates 19th-century British literature and character dynamics

Name: Languages and Culture Essay Prize (Trinity Cambridge)
Description: Essay contest exploring foreign languages, translation, and cross-cultural literature.
Evaluation_Criteria: Cross-cultural insight, linguistic nuance, critical evaluation of texts, Linguistically curious student preparing for modern language or comparative literature degrees

Name: LSE SU Economics Society Essay Competition
Description: Global essay contest hosted by the London School of Economics Student Union on world economics.
Evaluation_Criteria: Economic rigor, originality of argument, real-world empirical examples, Economics student able to craft well-researched arguments on contemporary economic shocks, ,
